# WO-2026-08-12-B15-VISION-04 — Round 4: fix what round 3 got wrong, more carefully

## Acceptance criteria

AC1 (= acceptance_property): **Make the dedup exclusion NON-authoritative.** Round 3's fix in
`resolveByCatalogue.js` correctly collapses two lines resolving to the same product+quantity, but
round 3's live run proved the identity it trusts (`matched_regular_id`) can itself be wrong — a
different, real product (Febreze Fabric Freshener) was misidentified as the same regular as a genuinely
different one (Lenor Outdoorable), and the "authoritative" exclusion silently deleted the real item.
**Change `excluded` to a review state (`needs_confirmation` or equivalent) whenever the two colliding
lines came from DIFFERENT source regions** — a same-region duplicate (the original Vanish case) is
still safe to auto-collapse (it's almost certainly the same physical handwriting read twice), but a
cross-region collision resolving to the same product is exactly the shape that can hide a genuine
misidentification, and must surface for a human decision, never silently vanish. Proven against the
EXACT captured Lenor/Febreze data from round 3's `run-b.json`.

AC2: **Investigate and address the dominant, still-unaddressed omission mode: partial misses within a
region that DOES produce lines** (distinct from the zero-line case round 3 already fixed). Round 3's own
new observability field (`initialSilentRegions`) proved this is real: a region can produce SOME lines
and still miss most of what's actually on it, with nothing in the current design able to detect that.
**One concrete, buildable direction to investigate, not a prescribed answer**: a cheap, deterministic,
model-free estimate of expected line density per region (e.g. counting distinct horizontal ink clusters
in the region's own image data) compared against how many lines the model actually returned for that
region — a large mismatch is itself a legitimate follow-up trigger, complementing the existing zero-line
trigger, without adding a routine per-line call. Investigate whether this or a better mechanism you find
is buildable within this WP's scope; if genuinely not buildable cheaply, report exactly why and what
would be needed, rather than shipping something that doesn't actually address the dominant failure mode
a third time.

AC3: **Investigate and fix the quantity-assertion collapse.** Round 3's `wrongQuantity: 0` result was an
artefact — the model asserted a quantity on only ~25% of lines (down from ~70-87% in round 2), not
because it got more accurate, but because it mostly stopped stating quantities at all. Trace this to
round 3's own prompt/schema changes (the quantity-evidence requirement from round 2, or the
no-prior-hallucination guard from round 3 — determine which, don't guess) and recalibrate: a quantity
should still be asserted whenever genuine evidence for it exists in the line's own text, exactly as
before round 3 — this WP must not trade "no wrong quantities" for "almost no quantities."

AC4: Re-verify, with a test reproducing the exact captured shape, that AC1's non-authoritative change
does not reintroduce the ORIGINAL Vanish-shaped same-region exact duplicate round 3 correctly fixed —
that specific case should remain auto-collapsed, only the cross-region case changes.

AC5: All touched-package tests pass with a non-zero executed count, including DB-gated tests via the
established disposable-Postgres pattern.
